title: cloud_fetch_results(): handle S3 rate limiting gracefully (retry/backoff, cap concurrency, don't silently drop results)
description:
## Summary

`cloud_fetch_results()` downloads one result tarball per reverse dependency. For large checks this puts hundreds of requests in flight at once, trips the backing S3 store's request-rate limit, and then **silently drops the throttled results** — producing a report that marks succeeded checks as "failed to check". This is a request to handle rate limiting gracefully.

## What happens

`cloud_fetch_results()` (`R/cloud.R`) creates a `curl` handle per revdep and runs them through a default `new_pool()`. With the default pool (HTTP/2 multiplexing, `host_con = 6`) that's effectively hundreds of concurrent requests. For a large check (e.g. ~2,300 revdeps) the burst trips S3's per-prefix rate limit; S3 returns `503 SlowDown`, which the API Gateway S3 proxy surfaces to the client as HTTP **`500`**.

The completion callback then does:

```r
handle_success <- function(res) {
  if (res$status_code >= 400) {
    unlink(out_file)   # delete and give up
  }
  cli_progress_update(id = pb)
}
```

Any `>= 400` (including the throttling `500`) just deletes the partial file and moves on — no retry, no backoff. The throttled results end up missing, so the subsequent `cloud_report()` / `cloud_summary()` shows those packages as "failed to check" with version `?`, even though the checks actually succeeded server-side.

A related trigger: `cloud_fetch_results()` iterates over `info$revdep_packages` (all revdeps) regardless of readiness, so running `cloud_report()` **before a check has finished** fans out requests for result objects that don't exist yet, which amplifies the burst.

Observed in practice: a ~2,300-revdep check produced ~2,300 HTTP 500s within a few seconds and an empty/misleading report, despite the checks themselves having succeeded.

## Suggested changes

1. **Retry transient failures with exponential backoff + jitter.** Treat `429`, `500`, `503`, and transport errors (add a `fail` callback to `multi_add()`) as retryable; treat `400`/`404` as "not available". Note `500` must be retryable here, because the API Gateway maps S3's `503 SlowDown` to `500`.
2. **Cap concurrency.** Use a bounded pool, e.g. `new_pool(total_con = 8, host_con = 8, multiplex = FALSE)`, instead of the default — so only a handful of requests are in flight and the rate limit isn't tripped in the first place.
3. **Only fetch results that are ready.** Filter to completed packages (e.g. via `cloud_job_status(job_name, "SUCCEEDED")`) before downloading, so calling `cloud_report()` before a check finishes doesn't request objects that don't exist yet.
4. **Surface incomplete downloads.** If some results still can't be fetched after retries, error/warn clearly ("N of M results couldn't be downloaded — re-run `cloud_fetch_results()`") instead of silently producing a report that says nothing was tested.

`cloud_fetch_results()` already resumes via `!file.exists(out_files)`, so re-runs only fetch what's missing — that pairs well with the above.

The service side could also help by returning `429` + `Retry-After` instead of an opaque `500`, but since the client currently has no retry at all, the client-side handling is needed regardless.

Happy to put up a PR if this direction sounds reasonable.

title: `cran_revdeps()` regex misses packages at field boundaries
description:
I've been doing some analysis of revdeps of usethis and devtools. It seem like they should have way fewer revdeps than they do! That is neither here not there, but just explains how I stumbled across this. I was seeing some pretty wild differences in revdep counts depending on exactly what I was looking at and how I went about it. And I found this bug.

---

`cran_revdeps_versions()` uses a regex to find reverse dependencies:

https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/blob/12dcbecda8278721ef7c75723eff2925eb1564fc/R/deps.R#L35

This requires a separator (`,`, `\n`, or a space) on **both** sides of the package name. It misses packages when the target appears at the start or end of a dependency field, or when a version constraint is directly adjacent with no space (e.g., `pkg(>= 1.0)`).

### Concrete examples

`cran_revdeps("usethis", dependencies = "Imports")` returns 69 packages, but `tools::package_dependencies()` finds 87 — 18 are silently dropped.

```r
rc <- revdepcheck::cran_revdeps("usethis", dependencies = "Imports")
truth <- tools::package_dependencies(
  "usethis", reverse = TRUE, which = "Imports"
)[[1]]
setdiff(truth, rc)
#>  [1] "bootCT"             "distops"            "doolkit"
#>  [4] "ensembleTax"        "FastUtils"          "fec16"
#>  [7] "IRTest"             "memoiR"             "OCSdata"
#> [10] "ontoFAST"           "OpenMindat"         "phrases"
#> [13] "polite"             "popbayes"           "positron.tutorials"
#> [16] "roxygen2md"         "rUM"                "Trendtwosub"
```

These packages really do list usethis in `Imports`, e.g.:

```r
ap <- available.packages()

ap["polite", "Imports"]
#> [1] "crayon, httr, memoise, ratelimitr, robotstxt (>= 0.6.0),\nrvest, usethis"

ap["OCSdata", "Imports"]
#> [1] "usethis (>= 2.0.0), purrr (>= 0.3.0), httr (>= 1.4.0)"

ap["fec16", "Imports"]
#> [1] "dplyr, readr, vroom, usethis"
```

The problem is that usethis is **last** in polite and fec16 (no trailing separator) and **first** in OCSdata (no leading separator). All three fail to match the regex.

### Why this hasn't been (much of) a problem in practice

Our typical workflow uses `revdep_check()` or `cloud_check()`, both of which pass multiple dependency types (the default is `c("Depends", "Imports", "Suggests", "LinkingTo")`). In `cran_revdeps_versions()`, the selected columns are pasted together with `,` before the regex is applied:

https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/blob/12dcbecda8278721ef7c75723eff2925eb1564fc/R/deps.R#L32-L34

This means a package that's last in Imports gets a `,` before the start of Suggests, which provides the missing separator. The multi-field paste papers over almost all boundary cases.

The one remaining edge case is a version constraint with no space, like `devtools(>= 2.2.2)`, where `(` is not one of the three recognized separators. In the multi-field case, this currently causes exactly 1 package to be missed (coronavirus, which lists `devtools(>= 2.2.2)` in Imports).

```r
ap["coronavirus", "Imports"]
#> [1] "devtools(>= 2.2.2)"
```

### Where it does bite

Calling `cran_revdeps()` with a single dependency type produces significantly undercounted results:

```r
library(revdepcheck)

truth <- function(pkg, which) {
  tools::package_dependencies(pkg, which = which, reverse = TRUE)[[1]]
}

length(cran_revdeps("devtools", dependencies = "Imports"))
#> 42
length(truth("devtools", "Imports"))
#> 70

length(cran_revdeps("devtools", dependencies = "Suggests"))
#> 296
length(truth("devtools", "Suggests"))
#> 476
```

title: `cloud_check()` should mercy kill a revdep that needs a package from a defunct repo
description: This is based on my recent experience doing revdepchecks for vroom. As of 2026-01-23, vroom has impactr as a revdep: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/impactr/index.html And here's its DESCRIPTION right now: ``` Package: impactr Title: Mechanical Loading Prediction Through Accelerometer Data Version: 0.4.1 Authors@R: person(given = "Lucas", family = "Veras", role = c("aut", "cre"), email = "lucasdsveras@gmail.com", comment = c(ORCID = "0000-0003-0562-5803")) Description: Functions to read, process and analyse accelerometer data related to mechanical loading variables. This package is developed and tested for use with raw accelerometer data from triaxial 'ActiGraph' accelerometers. License: MIT + file LICENSE URL: https://lveras.com/impactr/ BugReports: https://github.com/verasls/impactr/issues/ Encoding: UTF-8 LazyData: true Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE) RoxygenNote: 7.2.1 Imports: glue, lubridate, lvmisc, pillar, pracma, purrr, Rcpp, rlang (>= 0.4.6), signal, stringr, tibble, toOrdinal, utils, vroom Suggests: accdata, covr, knitr, rmarkdown, testthat (>= 3.0.0) Config/testthat/edition: 3 LinkingTo: Rcpp VignetteBuilder: knitr Language: en-GB Depends: R (>= 2.10) Additional_repositories: https://lveras.com/drat/ ``` It `Suggests` accdata, which is supposed to be available from the `Additional_repositories: https://lveras.com/drat/`. But that repository does not currently exist. ``` ~/work/vroom % curl -I https://lveras.com/drat/src/contrib/PACKAGES HTTP/2 403 alt-svc: h3=":8443"; ma=2592000 server: Caddy date: Sat, 24 Jan 2026 01:46:19 GMT ~/work/vroom % curl -I https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES HTTP/2 200 content-length: 5711710 date: Sat, 24 Jan 2026 01:46:59 GMT expires: Sat, 24 Jan 2026 02:16:59 GMT server: Apache/2.4.65 (Unix) last-modified: Sat, 24 Jan 2026 00:31:16 GMT etag: "57275e-6491764598047" accept-ranges: bytes cache-control: max-age=1800 x-cache: Miss from cloudfront via: 1.1 36d4ca7ddc4beff9d1b963574f5a4134.cloudfront.net (CloudFront) x-amz-cf-pop: YVR52-P3 x-amz-cf-id: 8Orpg5Pk3i4uJsa-iNH_gNdShgzquldFfQSZbpthkDiiuY13pgmJtA== ``` Here's how it looks when I try to install local dev deps with pak: ```r > pak::local_install_dev_deps() ✔ Loading metadata database ... done Run `[rlang::last_trace()](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Positron.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html#)` to see where the error occurred. Error: ! ! error in pak subprocess Caused by error: ! Could not solve package dependencies: * deps::/Users/jenny/tmp/impactr: Can't install dependency accdata * accdata: Can't find package called accdata. ``` In cloud revdep checks, this particular package seems to just hang, causing the entire job to be stuck at 1 thing still in progress and n - 1 things being complete. Eventually, somewhere north of 2 hours, something appears to time out and you can run `cloud_report()`, which does not report anything about this problematic package. I have a couple of wishes: * Can this doomed situation fail fast and be logged in the problems? Feels like it fits in the "failed to check" bucket. * Can we make it easier to find out which revdeps are still running? Part of what makes this situation tricky is that I can't see which package is the zombie. If I could, that unblocks me to do some local, artisanal troubleshooting. In this case, I have to wait 'til it's the only check still running, do `cloud_report()`, back out which packages have been checked, get the list of revdeps via `revdepcheck::cran_revdeps("vroom")`, then use `setdiff()` to figure out who's missing. * Given that this situation only generates a NOTE in CRAN's checks, should we be doing something different? title: Should `cloud_report_checklist()` just write itself to `revdep/checklist.md`?

title: improve robustness to untar2/incomplete block on file errors
description:
I realize this is a niche problem, but ... I'm trying to do a large revdep check (500+ packages) on a machine with a flaky network connection, and am frequently running into transient errors

> .Error in untar2(tarfile, files, list, exdir, restore_times) :  incomplete block on file

I currently have my `revdep_check()` call wrapped in a `repeat { r <- try(...); if (!inherits(r, "try-error")) break }` block, which helps a bit, but not enough — if a download fails before any of the workers has succeeded in fully checking a package, then that iteration of the loop doesn't make any progress.

I am willing to take a shot at hacking this myself but wouldn't mind opinions/input - in particular, I would like to implement (1) a few retries at downloading the package (seems easy enough) and (2) giving up and skipping further attempts (in the current `revdep_check()` invocation) to check the package that has failed to download.

title: What is the default for revdep_check(dependencies=), exactly?
description:
https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/blob/5a0c13819b83567a4c789311131d69dfa35a722c/R/revdepcheck.R#L39

`?revdep_check` is not clear enough here IMO:

https://revdepcheck.r-lib.org/reference/revdep_check.html

In R, a signature like this is somewhat ambiguous:

https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/blob/5a0c13819b83567a4c789311131d69dfa35a722c/R/revdepcheck.R#L59-L60

Because `match.arg()` often means "here's the `enum` of possible values, of which the first is chosen"; here that would mean "only downstream `Depends` are checked", which is "valid" but doesn't make that much sense. So I could _guess_ that the default is "any downstream `Depends`, `Imports`, `Suggests`, or `LinkingTo`", but it would be better to be more explicit here.

It's not even clear to me from a minute of reading the sources what the behavior is -- I have to jump to another package entirely to understand what's going on. All the more reason to be explicit in the doc page here.

title: revdep_check() installs some but not all Suggests:ed packages
description:
# Issue

I would expect it do to so, but `revdepcheck::revdep_check()` installs some but not all Suggests:ed packages.  This is not a new observation - I've had this "problem" since the very beginning (2 years?).  After running:

```r
library(revdepcheck)
revdep_check(bioc = TRUE, num_workers = 4L, quiet = FALSE)
revdep_report(all = TRUE)
```

the generated [revdep/problems.md](https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson/future/blob/67d1557abd80ad05ecfc5df3f84661a7c6c8872a/revdep/problems.md) reports on NOTEs such as:

> checking package dependencies ... NOTE
> ```
>   Package suggested but not available for checking: ‘DesignLibrary’
> ```

_Comment_: Some of the missing Suggests:ed packages reported are on non-mainstream repositories, so that's not surprising, but some of them are on CRAN and Bioconductor.

Specifically, for CRAN package [DeclareDesign](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/DeclareDesign/index.html) and Bioconductor package [methyvim](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/methyvim.html), I get the above NOTEs. I force a cached installation of these by calling
```r
crancache::install_packages(c("DesignLibrary", "minfiData"))
```
What I recall, I think neither of these were in the binary cache; they installed from source.

I now rerun revdepcheck:

```r
library(revdepcheck)
revdep_add(packages = c("DeclareDesign", "methyvim"))
revdep_check(bioc = TRUE, num_workers = 4L, quiet = FALSE)
revdep_report(all = TRUE)
```

title: Q: Parallel installation of the same packages, or not?
description:
Assume I have 10 packages, **pkg1**, **pkg2**, ..., **pkg10**, part of my reverse dependency check.  They all depend on a **dpkg** package, which is _not_ installed, and is not in the **crancache** cache.

How will **dpkg** be installed when I launch `revdepcheck::revdep_check()` in parallel with 20 workers?  Will it end up:

1. installing **dpkg** once and only once, or

2. will each parallel check task attempt to install **dpkg** independently?


Knowing how it works helps to decided whether it's beneficial to pre-install/pre-populate the **crancache** cache, before launching the revdep checks. Especially so when there are many revdep packages with common dependencies.

`revdepcheck::cloud_check()` was suggested by `usethis::use_release_issue()` when trying to release rsconnect (an rstudio/posit package).

I also found mentions of `RSTUDIO_CLOUD_REVDEP_KEY` while searching our internal Slack for `revdepcheck::cloud_check()` references. I eventually got the right answer (request a key) but the path was not obvious.

Could `revdepcheck::cloud_check()` check for the existence of `RSTUDIO_CLOUD_REVDEP_KEY` and produce a more helpful error?

title: WISH: `on_start()` "hook" function to tweak settings before launching each check
description:
# Background

Some packages fail sporadically due to race conditions when "old" and "new" are checked in parallel.  Common reasons are hard-coded TCP ports and shared file caches.  We may even have race conditions between packages checked if they share the same dependency.

When it comes to reverse-dependency checking, I consider these type of errors false positives.  Resolving them requires manual inspection and often rerunning the revdep checks for those packages sequentially.  This is a tedious and potentially error-prone process.


# Wish

Add a mechanism for calling a "hook" function just before `R CMD check` is launched.  When `revdep_check()` calls this function, it could pass the name of the package checked and whether 'old' or 'new' is checked.  This would allow me to do things like:

```r
revdep_check(on_start = function(pkg, version = c("old", "new"), ...) {
  ## Use a fresh BiocFileCache folder specific to the current check
  path <- file.path(tempdir(), pkg, version)
  dir.create(path, recursive = TRUE)
  Sys.setenv(BFC_CACHE = path)
})
```

title: Re-enable checking of vignettes?
description:
Hi, I just ran into a case where CRAN's incoming reverse-dependency checks caught a bug in my submitted package that revealed itself only in a vignette in one of the 138 reverse-depency packages.  

After some troubleshooting, I figured out that `revdepcheck:revdep_check()` skips the vignettes for its checks;

https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/blob/61ab33e6adc3cfcb5d51012b8ad7e94fd99a092c/R/check.R#L32

I don't see an obvious way to re-enable vignette checks.  Could you please add this as an argument that can be overridden, e.g. `args = c("--no-manual", "--no-build-vignettes")`?

title: revdep_check should fail gracefully when it times out & tell the user to increase `timeout`
description:
When doing reverse dependency checks of my gratia package, `revdep_check()` times out as soon as the installation of all packages needed to check the dependencies and gratia is completed. This is what I see:

```r
> revdepcheck::revdep_check(num_workers = 4)

description:
I just had a fairly successful cloud revdep run with usethis. But one of the two packages that failed is named "do" (which seems like a bad idea, but that is beside the point).

Reporting failure for this package, specifically, seems to be a problem. I'm not sure if it's something about how it fails or ... could it somehow have something to do with it's name?

Here's my `revdep/` directory right after this run:

https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/tree/ded1495b6489e93e1ec88e1ad117f7f4c2d6b2fc/revdep

In `cran.md`, it inexplicably is not reported alongside the other failure (butcher https://github.com/tidymodels/butcher/issues/201).

title: revdep folder should be added to buildignore
description:
Launching the `revdepcheck::revdep_check(num_workers = 4)` function will create a folder at the root of the package called `revdep`. 

This folder is not added to the buildignore, so following the worflow from `usethis::use_release_issue` makes the submitted package fail, because we do the checks before the revdeps, but if not buildignored, the CRAN submission fails. 

```
 + [ ] devtools::check(remote = TRUE, manual = TRUE) # ok
 + [ ]  devtools::check_win_devel() # ok
  + [ ] rhub::check_for_cran() # ok
  + [ ] revdepcheck::revdep_check(num_workers = 4)  # no longer ok but we don't recheck according to the checklist
  + [ ] Update cran-comments.md
  + [ ] git push

Submit to CRAN:

  + [ ] usethis::use_version('patch')
 + [ ]  devtools::submit_cran()
 ```

title: Detect github API remotes
description:
I just had a cloud check run where all packages failed because I forgot to change the remote to use URL form. When this happens, the cloud report does not contain any information about the failure. The `new` folders are completely missing from the results.

To avoid this, `cloud_check()` could detect non-url remotes in the description file and refuse to run if any is detected, with a suggestion to use url form instead. Or perhaps it could generate url remotes automatically before building the tarball?

description:
I ran revdepcheck on the ggnewscale package and it failed to checked 12/36 packages. `revdep/README.md` listed those failures, but `revdep/problems.md` stated that there were "no problems at all", while `revdep/failures.md` listed installation failures (of the `cannot open URL` variety) for only some of the problematic packages. `revdep/cran.md` stated that no packages were failed to check. 

I'm not sure how to make a reproducible example. Perhaps cloning https://github.com/eliocamp/ggnewscale/tree/dev and running `revdepcheck::revdep_check()`.

title: Regular CRAN checks for tidyverse deprecations
description:
With the latest changes to lifecycle and testthat, you should only ever discover soft deprecations when actively developing your package (and most regular deprecations won't cause a CRAN failure). But there are lots of packages that are not actively developed, and it would be nice to have some way to gently notify those maintainers that they're using functions that we no longer recommend.

I was thinking that every 6 months, we could run all tests and examples for all packages that depend on a tidyverse package, collect and summarise all the deprecations, and email the maintainer. It would be a purely informative email since no action would be required, but it means that folks will here from us 2-4 times before we move from a soft deprecation to a regular deprecation, or a regular deprecation to defunct.

title: cran_revdeps_versions internal bugged
description:
Hi,

today I found out that the `cran_revdeps_versions` helper that is used by `revdep_init` is bugged and incorrectly determinates reverse dependencies if there are two packages following the naming convention `pkgA` and `pkgA.something`. I'll show it using the `admiral` cran package as an example.

```
> revdepcheck:::cran_revdeps_versions("admiral")
       package version
1      admiral   0.8.1
2   admiraldev   0.1.0
3  admiralonco   0.1.0
4       xportr   0.1.0
5 admiral.test   0.3.0
```

it doesn't take much time to realize that this list is definitely faulty. It contains the package itself (`admiral`) which obviously should not happen as the package cannot be its own dependency.  Further, inspection showcase other problems. Both `admiraldev` and `admiral.test` are not reverse dependencies of `admiral`, quite the contrary, it is `admiral` to import them.

I've investigated the issue and I believe it comes from the fault regexp in the following line: 
https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/blob/main/R/deps.R#L23

it is supposed to mach an entire word, but for regexp dot splits the word, meaning `\badmiral\b` will be matched not only to `admiral` but also to `admiral.test` which should not be the case. That's why `admiral` and `admiraldev` appeared in the list as they depend on `admiral.test` which was mistakenly classified as `admiral`.

This renders revdepcheck of `admiral` (and similar packages with the same convention) impossible, as the source against we check is removed after it was checked against... admiral itself. Meaning packages checked later cannot find the installation. 

The fix could be connected to do enhancement of the previous line https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/blob/main/R/deps.R#L22. If you remove the package name from that 'super-string' it should be easier to write an appropriate regexp, now we kinda fall in a danger zone when the package could match itself.

Hopefully, my explanation is clear. Let me know if I can help you anyhow with solving that.

title: revdep_reset fails to reset
description:
Running the latest version (revdepcheck 1.0.0.9001) on Windows 10 and R3.6.0, I find that `revdep_reset` is not fully operational.

`revdep_check` had completed, but had failed to check one package.  I fixed the issue that prevented that package from checking, then ran revdep_reset.

`revdepcheck::revdep_check` returns
```
* See results of previous run in 'revdep/README.md'
* Reset for another run with `revdepcheck::revdep_reset()`
```

After running `revdepcheck::revdep_reset(path/to/package)`, this message still persists on revdep_check.  The package's `revdep` folder contains `data.sqlite` and the three 'md' files (README, failures, problems), but the `checks` directory has been deleted.  
I cannot manually delete `data.sqlite`, because Windows recognizes it as being 'in use' by the R session. 
If I close R, then manually delete the revdep directory, then revdep_check works as expected.

Possibly related: If I interrupt revdep_check (with `Esc` keypress) then it exits with 
```
Warning message:
call dbDisconnect() when finished working with a connection 
```
It resumes on revdep_check(), and revdep_reset does not throw an error.

title: revdepcheck against repository different than CRAN
description:
Hi

first of all, I'd like to thank you a lot for your marvelous under this package. I think it really makes developer life easier.

I find it difficult to use `revdepcheck` for my use case and wanted to ask you whether it is possible or is planned to be possible in the near future. I'm building a company-wide CRAN-like repository of R packages. I wanted the reverse dependencies to check to be part of the submissions process that happens prior to updating the package in this repository. The most important part of this check is performing it in isolation from CRAN, checks should only be executed against packages available in my custom repository.  Is it possible to do such a thing with the vanilla version of revdepcheck? If not, can I do it in finite time by forking this package and altering a few lines? It seems like caching `options(repos)` or even masking CRAN with a link to my custom repo changes nothing.

I see revdepcheck as a great tool that makes the developer work much easier, but I find it pretty limiting that it hardcodes and assumes CRAN as the target repo disallowing custom ones.

Best
Szymon Maksymiuk

title: Better detect check error differences between CRAN and dev check
description:
We had some issue detected on CRAN that we missed using revdepcheck comparison. 

It happens because the comparison if made as a difference in check results (old vs new) and both case had an issue when ran in revdepcloud check. 
```
* checking re-building of vignette outputs ... WARNING
```

However, 
* the revdep package checked had no issue on CRAN, which currently revdepcheck does not know about
* the specific error was not the same in both case.

Regarding the latter, the issue was because some LaTeX packages are missing the cloud service  
````
Error: processing vignette 'BENMMI_User_Manual.Rnw' failed with diagnostics:
Running 'texi2dvi' on 'BENMMI_User_Manual.tex' failed.
LaTeX errors:
! LaTeX Error: File `colortbl.sty' not found.

Type X to quit or <RETURN> to proceed,
or enter new name. (Default extension: sty)

! Emergency stop.
<read *> 
````

but error with the new version of the package was 
````
Error: processing vignette 'BENMMI_User_Manual.Rnw' failed with diagnostics:
Running 'texi2dvi' on 'BENMMI_User_Manual.tex' failed.
LaTeX errors:
! LaTeX Error: Option clash for package xcolor.

See the LaTeX manual or LaTeX Companion for explanation.
Type  H <return>  for immediate help.
 ...                                              
! LaTeX Error: File `sectsty.sty' not found.

Type X to quit or <RETURN> to proceed,
or enter new name. (Default extension: sty)

! Emergency stop.
<read *> 
````

which is a different error.  This part was the one we should have detected and was raised on CRAN

````
LaTeX errors:
! LaTeX Error: Option clash for package xcolor.
````

If the CTAN packages were available on the cloud service, this would not have been an issue, but still I think improving the report to detect such differences in errors during check would help. 

About revdepcloud issue with CTAN packages, see related https://github.com/rstudio/revdepcheck-cloud/issues/87

title: Retrieve current CRAN check results to flag a different revdepcheck result
description:
Related to https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/issues/331

Currently, I don't think **revdepcheck** will in any case retrieve current CRAN check results for a reverse dependency check.

This would be an interesting information to detect some errors in the revdepcheck process as currently only old vs new differences are reported. However, it is possible like in #331 that old results are not similar to current CRAN check results and could lead to missed issues.

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: Overzealous definition of "dependency error"
description:
@jimhester recently set `_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_="false"` in our cloud revdep checks, at my request, because a revdep has a soft dependency on a Bioconductor package: the usethis revdep butcher Suggests NMF, which is on Bioconductor.

This leads to `butcher/dependency_install.log` to contain this ERROR message:
```
ERROR: dependency 'Biobase' is not available for package 'NMF'
```

However butcher **can** still be installed and checked. But I can't inspect those details via `cloud_details(revdep = "butcher")` because `cloud_compare()` still interprets this as a dependency error and we end up here:

https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/blob/db3bc3b3667db4f93b63ff2e87a3c5608feafa81/R/cloud.R#L342-L344

```
> cloud_details(revdep = "butcher")
══ Reverse dependency check ══════════════════════════════════════════ butcher  ══

Status: 

Error in if (nrow(rows) == 0) { : argument is of length zero
Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.
> lt
<error/rlang_error>
Error in if (nrow(rows) == 0) { : argument is of length zero
Backtrace:
    █
 1. ├─(function (x, ...) ...
 2. └─revdepcheck::print.revdepcheck_details(x)
 3.   ├─base::print(structure(x, class = "rcmdcheck_comparison"), header = FALSE) /Users/jenny/rrr/revdepcheck/R/results.R:53:2
 4.   └─rcmdcheck:::print.rcmdcheck_comparison(...)
 5.     └─rcmdcheck:::print_comparison(x, -1, "Fixed")
```

It's a printing problem, i.e. this leads to the formation of  an unexpected or malformed object of class `rcmdcheck_error`.

I'm not sure which solution(s) is/are correct:

* Detect that we successfully installed and checked butcher, despite the failure to install NMF
* Construct a (more) valid `rcmdcheck_error` object by having a component named `cmp` [here](https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/blob/04fe3906e5a9eced516183fea4c0f4df3a5de102/R/compare.R#L12)
* Make `rcmdcheck:::print_comparison` resilient to the absence of `x$cmp`

title: C stack usage too close to the limit when using strsplit on a 00check.log content
description:
This is the error I get when using `cloud_report()` or `cloud_summary()`. It comes from `cloud_results()` when parsing results to compare them. 

It took me time to isolate from where it comes. It happens at this line : 
https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/blob/31cadc35b3c8b58690cd73bb662cc24c96bbb9a3/R/cloud.R#L328

This is causing issue with one specific package, but it make the whole process fails. 
`00check.log` contains a big number of line (27565), and specifically a very long entry because the checks have failed during vignette building. It happens with package StanHeaders - extract from the content: 
````
* checking running R code from vignettes ... NONE
  ‘stanmath.Rmd’ using ‘UTF-8’... OK
* checking re-building of vignette outputs ... WARNING
Error(s) in re-building vignettes:
--- re-building ‘stanmath.Rmd’ using rmarkdown
In file included from /opt/R/4.0.3/lib/R/site-library/RcppEigen/include/Eigen/Core:397,
                 from /opt/R/4.0.3/lib/R/site-library/RcppEigen/include/Eigen/Dense:1,
                 from /opt/R/4.0.3/lib/R/site-library/RcppEigen/include/RcppEigenForward.h:30,
                 from /opt/R/4.0.3/lib/R/site-library/RcppEigen/include/RcppEigen.h:25,
                 from file828956d1b8e3.cpp:3:
/opt/R/4.0.3/lib/R/site-library/RcppEigen/include/Eigen/src/Core/arch/SSE/PacketMath.h:60:39: warning: ignoring attributes on template argument ‘__m128’ {aka ‘__vector(4) float’} [-Wignored-attributes]
   60 | template<> struct is_arithmetic<__m128>  { enum { value = true }; };
      |                                       ^
/opt/R/4.0.3/lib/R/site-library/RcppEigen/include/Eigen/src/Core/arch/SSE/PacketMath.h:61:40: warning: ignoring attributes on template argument ‘__m128i’ {aka ‘__vector(2) long long int’} [-Wignored-attributes]
   61 | template<> struct is_arithmetic<__m128i> { enum { value = true }; };
      |                                        ^
/opt/R/4.0.3/lib/R/site-library/RcppEigen/include/Eigen/src/Core/arch/SSE/PacketMath.h:62:40: warning: ignoring attributes on template argument ‘__m128d’ {aka ‘__vector(2) double’} [-Wignored-attributes]
   62 | template<> struct is_arithmetic<__m128d> { enum { value = true }; };
      |                                        ^

/opt/R/4.0.3/lib/R/site-library/RcppEigen/include/Eigen/src/Core/arch/SSE/PacketMath.h:161:43: warning: ignoring attributes on template argument ‘Eigen::internal::Packet4f’ {aka ‘__vector(4) float’} [-Wignored-attributes]
  161 | template<> struct unpacket_traits<Packet4f> { typedef float  type; enum {size=4, alignment=Aligned16}; typedef Packet4f half; };
      |                                           ^
/opt/R/4.0.3/lib/R/site-library/RcppEigen/include/Eigen/src/Core/arch/SSE/PacketMath.h:162:43: warning: ignoring attributes on template argument ‘Eigen::internal::Packet2d’ {aka ‘__vector(2) double’} [-Wignored-attributes]
  162 | template<> struct unpacket_traits<Packet2d> { typedef double type; enum {size=2, alignment=Aligned16}; typedef Packet2d half; };
````

This goes one from line 70 to the end. As the file is supposed to be splitted by entry `* `, I believe this creates a string way to big. 

I have joined the log file here: [00check.log](https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/files/7541278/00check.log)

To reproduce: 

```r
url <- "https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/files/7541278/00check.log"
tmp_file <- tempfile()
download.file(url, destfile = tmp_file)

stdout <- brio::read_file(tmp_file)
stdout <- iconv(stdout, "UTF-8", "UTF-8", sub = "bytes")
stdout <- gsub("\r\n", "\n", stdout, fixed = TRUE)
entries <- strsplit(paste0("\n", stdout), "\n\\*+[ ]")[[1]][-1]

unlink(tmp_file)
```

It throws this error on the line `entries <-`
```
Error: C stack usage  23362914 is too close to the limit
```

If we can discuss why we get this very long error during the vignette build, it would be interesting to handle this special case somehow. 
At least by using a `tryCatch()` to not stop the whole process, and report that this packages has not been compared because of parsing failure to investigate. What do you think ? 

For the context, I found this in my undergoing work of trying to understand and make the revdepcloud service works better for using it, including with vignette build. `StandHeaders` package doesn't error on CRAN, so it should not in our ecosystem either. but that is another story.

title: Checking broken packages on cloud
description:
To check broken packages we currently need to be careful to add the failures to the set to test, otherwise they will disappear from the report (which is particularly problematic if these failures are caused by the dev version of the package):

```r
pkgs <- cloud_broken(job, install_failures = TRUE, timeout_failures = TRUE)
cloud_check(revdep_packages = pkgs)
```

It seems it would be safer and more practical to make `cloud_broken()` return failures by default, then it's just:

```r
cloud_check(revdep_packages = cloud_broken(job))
```

Alternatively this could be wrapped in a `cloud_recheck()` function.

```r
cloud_recheck <- function(job_id = cloud_job()) {
  pkgs <- cloud_broken(job_id, install_failures = TRUE, timeout_failures = TRUE)
  cloud_check(revdep_packages = pkgs)
}
```

cc @jimhester

title: cloud_report() should report packages that didn't get checked
description: Because the jobs were never run

title: `cloud_status()` should report elapsed time looking at finished time when it is done
description:
Currently, `cloud_status()` will report elapsed time by comparing created time and current time when the function is ran / called
https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/blob/508e5356ec67d33d1402ae116e03164ce379ebd8/R/cloud.R#L37-L38

When the jobs are done, ETA is passed to done, but the finished time is not used. The new API allow to have this information 
https://github.com/rstudio/revdepcheck-cloud#monitor-your-job

* status of the job will pass to `finished`
* `finished_timestamp` field will have a value. 

I think this value could be used to get in `cloud_status()` the correct elapsed time.

title: cloud checks are missing cases when the vignettes fail to build
description: E.g. if a failure happens when building a vignette this is not correctly reported as a failure.

title: Somehow include failed builds in the `cloud_summary()` and `cloud_broken()`
description:
Unfortunately sometimes AWS preempts jobs and kills them, which results in uninformative failures.

Compounding this problem is currently we don't include these failures in the `cloud_summary()` or `cloud_report()`, so depending on which jobs failed you might not know a regression occurred.

As the only thing we can really do is re-run these jobs we need to have a function to query which ones failed.

title: Warn if running cloud checks with GitHub remotes and 1000s  of checks
description:
You can easily exhaust the PAT if you are trying to check a development package with a GitHub remote. A workaround is to use a URL remote as mentioned in the vignette https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/blob/bcdf424ebc3adc279d6198f32cb4317507e7fac3/vignettes/cloud.Rmd#L41

But this is easy to forget.

We could instead issue a warning if you try to check a package with a GitHub remote and lots of reverse dependencies.

title: Error using `revdepcheck::revdep_check()` and `devtools::revdep_check()`
description:
I'm trying to upload [my first CRAN package](https://github.com/filipezabala/voice), but I'm stuck on checking all downstream/reverse dependencies. 

I'm doing everything as the [second edition of Hadley Wickham's book](https://r-pkgs.org/) suggests. I solved all pending issues indicated by `devtools::check()`, however I'm not able to make the verification of reverse dependencies using the functions `devtools::revdep_check()` and `revdepcheck::revdep_check()` as suggested by Mr. Wickham.

With `devtools::revdep_check()` I have the following error:

```
> devtools::revdep_check()
Error: 'revdep_check' is not an object exported from 'namespace: devtools'
```

With `revdepcheck::revdep_check()` the following appears:

```
> revdepcheck::revdep_check(num_workers = 4)
── INSTALL ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 2 versions ──
Installing CRAN version of voice
Error: (converted from warning) package ‘voice’ is not available for this version of R

A version of this package for your version of R might be available elsewhere,
see the ideas at
https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-patched/R-admin.html#Installing-packages
```
Running R 4.0.3 on macOS Catalina 10.15.7 also with all packages updated to latest CRAN releases.
```

I'm probably doing something wrong, but I can't figure out what it is. I also posted on [this link](https://community.rstudio.com/t/revdepcheck-problems/28305), any help is welcome.

Bonus: When I tried to install via `install.packages('revdepcheck', dep=T)`:

The solution was to install directly from GitHub:

Best regards,

description:
There are two issues here: (1) disconnecting from some database used in `revedep_check()` and (2) cleaning up the `revdep/` folder.

(1) When I run `revdep_check()` on a package I get a message to disconnect from some database using `dbDisconnect()`
What package?  I tried `DBI::dbDisconnect()`, but that failed. Please make this message more explicit.

    -- REPORT --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Writing summary to 'revdep/README.md'
    Writing problems to 'revdep/problems.md'
    Writing failures to 'revdep/failures.md'
    Warning message:
    call dbDisconnect() when finished working with a connection 
    > dbDisconnect()
    Error in dbDisconnect() : could not find function "dbDisconnect"
    > DBI::dbDisconnect()
    Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  : 
      unable to find an inherited method for function ‘dbDisconnect’ for signature ‘"missing"’

(2) `revdep_check()` leaves all its' files in the `revdep/` folder, but it is not clear what to do with them wrt `git` and `github`.

- run `revdep_reset()` after a clean check?
- add a `.gitignore` entry for `revdep/` ?
- ...


I was just burned by a `revdep/` folder in the repo from a past release. Trying to run `revdep_reset()`  kept failing, 
Could not delete `data.sqlite`.

title: Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)) :    error in evaluating the argument 'statement' in selecting a method for function 'dbExecute': invalid multibyte string, element 1
description:
Running the 2020-12-27 dev version of revdepcheck today on Windows 10, I twice got this error:
```
[0/34] 00:02:08 | ETA:  ?s | (4) ballr [I], BARIS [I], BFS [CC]Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)) : 
  error in evaluating the argument 'statement' in selecting a method for function 'dbExecute': invalid multibyte string, element 1
```
Causing the process to stop.  In each case, I removed the latest-listed package from the check and restarted the check.  In this case that command was `revdep_rm(pkg = ".", "BFS")`.  In the end, I only had to do this twice on a 34-package check.

If it's hard to resolve this, it would be acceptable behavior for it to warn or skip that package - the stopping the check is the rough part, since I've usually stepped away while the process runs.

title: WISH: Make it possible to rerun only 'new' while keeping 'old' results
description:
Say you run revdepcheck to just find a small bug, which you then fix.  When you then run revdepcheck again a few moments later, it'll rerun both 'old' and 'new' checks, although the 'old' ones will produce identical `R CMD check` output as the first run.

I'd like to propose a mechanism for `revdep_check()` to keep existing 'old' results and just rerun the 'new' ones.

For this to be solid, I guess it needs to make sure that none of the revdep packages and none of their dependencies have been updated since the previous run.  If they have, then those cached results should be invalidated triggering a rerun of 'old' for the invalidated revdep packages.

The above strategy should decrease the processing time significantly, even if there are a few updates in the revdep DAG.

title: Remotes field in DESCRIPTION doesn't propagate to revdeps
description:
I wanted to run revdeps for furrr, which currently relies on the development version of globals. I have put a Remote on globals in the DESCRIPTION file of furrr. It seems that `revdep_check()` won't respect the fact that I want the dev version of globals when it installs the dependencies for each revdep.

I have installed the development version of globals locally with `devtools::install_github("HenrikBengtsson/globals@develop")`. The dev version is `0.12.5-9000`.

It does not look like this updated the cache in crancache, which might be the problem? I can confirm this with:

```r
> pkgs <- crancache::crancache_list()
> pkgs[pkgs$Package == "globals", ]
    Package    Repository Version                           MD5sum
862 globals cran/platform  0.12.5 f792524b7ec8ab80267ece9c154ff511
```

I stepped through `revdep_check()` and it looks like it uses crancache for installing deps of the revdep packages.

One of the revdeps is simhelpers, and it failed because of an issue that was fixed in dev globals. I can further confirm that the CRAN version of globals was used because it is in `/revdep/library.noindex/simhelpers/globals/` and the DESCRIPTION file there shows 0.12.5.

title: Use one package library per package?
description:
This gives both isolation and performance: Each package is installed only once, into its dedicated package library. Each worker then uses a unique `.libPaths()`, which may be very long.

I'm tempted to start a new package "multilib" for the purpose of managing such split package libraries, but I wanted to double-check first if this is the scope of pkgman or perhaps another package I'm missing.  The "multilib" package would offer replacements for `library()` and `require()` that temporarily change `.libPaths()` so that all dependencies can be found, and also an entry point to compute library paths so that a particular package with all of its declared dependencies is available. It would also need an `install()` entry point.

## Performance test

I've made a few quick checks on my local package library of ~800 packages. First, I created 800 package libraries, all in `~/R-separate`, where each corresponds to one package:

```sh
ls -d ~/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.4/* |
  sed -r 's#^(.*)/([^/]*)$#echo \2; mkdir -p R-separate/\2; ln -s \1/\2 R-separate/\2/\2#' |
  sh
```

(Replace the last `sh` with `head` or `less` to see what's going on before running.)

Then, I tested the performance of `library(tidyverse)` with both my regular and the split library:

### Flat library

``` r
system.time(suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse)))
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>   1.272   0.136   1.409
```

### Split library

``` r
.libPaths(dir("~/R-separate/", full.names = TRUE))
system.time(suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse)))
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>   1.264   0.156   1.426
```

This seems to scale, at least for 800 packages.

title: failed detection of S3 method masking problem
description:
I recently ran into a problem with a CRAN submission that was undetected by `revdep_check()`, I think because of an environment/order-of-package-loading issue.

`car` has had an `influence.merMod` S3 method for a while; `lme4` just added one with incompatible arguments/output format. No problems were detected with `revdep_check()`, I assume/guess because `lme4` was loaded *before* `car`, so that the `car` version of the method masked the `lme4` version.  In contrast, the CRAN checks gave an error - I assume because package/method loading occurred in the other order, so the `lme4` version ended up being called by the `car` examples.

Thoughts, ideas about how to address this? It will presumably depend in a sensitive way on whether fresh R sessions (with only the basic/built-in S3 methods registered) are started for each check ... to my knowledge it's very difficult to unregister S3 methods/restore a 'clean' S3 method list ...

title: Checking revdeps of R
description:
Before submitting a patch to R core, it's sometimes needed to check for issues against CRAN packages (all of CRAN or just a sufficiently large sample, depending on the patch).

It might be possible to check old and new R simultaneously, but it is probably hard to make this work portably.

Alternatively, the packages could be checked on old R first and then on new R. Then it's up to the user to change the currently active R version between the checks. As discussed in #198, this needs one library per checked package to ensure nothing changes between old and new checks. Or perhaps installing all deps first would work, as discussed in #33.

title: Suggestion:  run revdep checks in random order
description:
If packages have a lot of reverse dependencies, `revdep_check()` can take a really long time to run.  (For example, `rgl` has 322 revdeps, and when I ran my own revdep code, it took 15 hours to complete.  `revdep_check` estimates 2 days after doing a couple.)  

It would be nice if it did the checks in a random order instead of alphabetically:  then if I quit after a couple of hours, at least I will have seen a random subsample, instead of the same alphabetical subsample as the previous time.

title: Allow more flexible creation of tasks
description:
Poking through the code a bit, it looks like the notion of "tasks" is how the workers actually get spawned / managed. If it is possible to either

(1) create a generic `tasks` R6 class that has the appropriate methods (farming those out to `processx` by default) for task management
(2) allow `processx` to implement a more generic task backend

That would be great! Then I would expect users could provide their own tasks implementation, etc. Specifically, I am thinking about the following backends:

- background jobs in the RStudio IDE. This is a very nice way for even a single system to spawn and monitor the many tasks/jobs that may be generated here
- launcher jobs in RStudio Server Pro. If the RStudio Server Pro cluster is using a Kubernetes or Slurm cluster to launch R sessions, then it is possible that this feature would allow the `revdepcheck` access to many more resources than are available otherwise for parallelism. Further, we get some nice functionality within the IDE to manage this
- there are almost certainly other backends that people would like to use for HPC / distributed checking as well.

If this issue belongs upstream in `processx`, I'm happy to move it there!

title: Documentation, please.

title: Consider producing individual package reports
description:
Instead of one giant `problems.md`.

This would make life easier for large packages like testthat, and give more space to inline all test failures.

title: Including more test output in reports
description:
* Check that these files are saved in the database
* Save complete test file and link to it from `problems.md`?

title: Ensure database captures all data needed for report
description:
* Platform details - should be captured during `revdep_init()`
* `libraries.csv` - should be captured `revdep_install()`.

Will need new database tables, and new helpers to retrieve the results.

title: Re-run checks on just dev version
description: If you're re-checking the revdeps because you've made a change to your package, you shouldn't need to re-run the checks for the CRAN version.

title: Reduce duplication in print.revdepcheck_details vs failure_details
description:
* Need to have user facing `max_lines()` option
* Should be moved to rcmdcheck?

title: Graphics output
description:
Some packages fail, because they try to use `tcltk`, or plot to the default graphics device.
We need a workaround for these, e.g. an alternate graphics device, or a headless X server might work.

I don't know what happens to these on Windows.

title: Set NOT_CRAN to true for the checks ?
description: Maybe optionally?

title: Report results by group
description:
For packages like rlang, the higher order revdeps of dplyr, purrr, and tidyr must be checked in addition to the first order revdeps of rlang. As discussed in #198, these can be added manually to the DB.

It'd be helpful to add support for groups in the DB so these additional revdeps can be reported separately, either by adding a group column to the summary table, or by producing different summary files for each group.

title: Do not mark package as done if only old/new is done
Better display of install failures
description: i.e. inline the failure text into the problems report

title: feature request: revdep_skip() ?
description:
As a way around the problems described in https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck/issues/87 , and more broadly for dealing with packages that are problematic in some as-yet-unforeseen way, it would be nice if there were a `revdep_skip()` that did the opposite of `revdep_add()`, i.e. denoted a set of packages to ignore when checking.

Sorry if a way to do this already exists and I've missed it.

title: Set check options for revdeps to skip latex rendering
description:
It would be great if there was a way either in `revdepcheck` or `rcmdcheck` to set check parameters. I would like to run revdep checks on a machine without latex, so I need: `CMD check`:

```
--no-manual --no-build-vignettes
```

Note that this still tests the vignette R code, it just doesn't render the final html / pdf. I think this makes sense, latex/pandoc rendering problems are always false positives due to missing latex packages. It is very unlikely a result of changes in dependencies.

title: Better API to manipulate the build queue
description: E.g. list packages, remove them, add them, etc.

title: Practical advice on usage
description:
I'd like to record what I did most recently. Maybe it would be helpful to give advice somewhere? Or you can close this issue and I can re-search it up when I need it 😁

I think this is basically good advice and it mattered a lot trying to do revdep checks in a place with incredibly bad internet.

Run R in the shell, as opposed to an/the instance of RStudio open to the target package. In general, suppress your personal startup behaviour.

I needed to keep my computer awake for loooooong periods of time so I also used the macOS caffeinate feature:

```
caffeinate -i R --vanilla
```

In R, I used `.libPaths("path/to/my/library/for/non-base-or-recommended-packages")` to add my personal library to the search path, so I could use revdepcheck.

In general, do this:
``` r
revdep_check(num_workers = 4)
```

If there are problem packages that keep timing out and holding on to a worker (I see this is now fixed #183), note their names. Kill the job. Explicitly remove the problem packages like so:

``` r
revdepcheck:::revdep_rm(".", c("BIOMASS", "cartools", "rstantools"))
```

Restart with multiple workers. When things stall, note more problem packages. Lather, rinse, repeat until you get through the bulk of the job.

Now tackle the problem packages one at a time with a really long timeout.

``` r
revdepcheck::revdep_add(".", "BIOMASS")
revdep_check(pkg = ".", quiet = FALSE, timeout = as.difftime(60, units = "mins"))
```

title: Installation error status
description:
While checking, installation errors are not showing the red "I" like they use to.

Adding installation error packages with `revdepcheck::revdep_add_broken(install_failures = TRUE)` does not add the packages.

Installation errors are not printed in problems.md by default.  (This may be changed behavior though.  If it is, they should not have a dead link from the `README.md` file.)

My current status information:
```r
revdepcheck:::report_revdeps("shiny")$status %>% unique()
#> [1] "+"  "i+"
```

All pkgs with the status value of `i+` are the pkgs with installation failure.

Please let me know if I can provide any more information.

title: A revdep that never times out
description: I reran usethis's revdep checks over night. This is about a 30 minute job. One particular package is problematic (BIOMASS) and it sits on a worker and never goes anywhere, never times out. Here's what the end of the run looked like in the morning: I've rerun the checks several times over the past few weeks and this behaviour with this package is consistent. So whatever way it hangs or fails is somehow beyond the reach of what revdepcheck does to kill things.

description: Rather than interleaving with `problems.md`

description: It would be useful to have an easy way to just test the packages that have been added to CRAN since the last run. (This is useful for testthat which gains ~10 new revdeps per week)

title: Use latest download tarball to check
description:
In case a package is updated on CRAN, and the checks are restarted. 

Half-finished checks are re-run, since #198 is fixed, so it is very unlikely that old and new would run with different versions.

title: Stable columns in the progress bar
description:
When you are running multiple packages in parallel it is useful to know which version of a package is at which stage (old vs new). e.g.

`pkgname [CC]`

Indicates that both versions are running R CMD check. However once one has finished it is changed to

`pkgname [C]`

So it is not possible to tell which of the two builds is done. It would be useful to show something like

`pkgname [_C]` or `pkgname [ C]`

So you could see that the old check has finished, but the new version is still running, or vise versa.

title: Parallel processing: Race conditions between "old" and "new" checks
description:
# Issue
I see inconsistent results when running revdep multiple times (the exact same pkg and revdep pkg versions).  For some runs a package may show an error in "new", sometimes in "old", sometimes in "both", and sometimes in neither.   To resolve this I've found myself doing a `revdep_add(package = redo_pkg)` and restart until both "new" and "old" pass.

I haven't traced the exact reason for this, but an intelligent guess is that some packages request a resources such as a fixed port number that both "new" and "old" try to acquire, i.e. there's a race condition between the two `R CMD check`:s of the same package.

# Suggestion
A possible workaround for race conditions between "new" and "old" is to minimize the risk of them running at the same time.  This could be done by first running "new" for all packages and then "old" for the same packages.   Another way would be to always to "new" and "old" sequentially, with the downside that when testing a small number of packages all cores may not be fully utilized but that should be less of a problem when there's a large number of packages to be tested.

There could of course still be race conditions on shared resources across packages, but the risk for that should be lower than within packages.

description:
See this [SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/46365317/what-is-the-most-user-friendly-way-to-test-the-reverse-dependencies-for-a-packag#) thread posted September of 2017. I'm experience the same issue. I have a Windows machine and am running the newest version of R (v3.5.0) and RStudio (v1.1.453). 
Any suggestions would be helpful. Thanks

title: Don't show unrelated problems
description: I.e. errors that are the same before and after. Maybe optionally. In the report.

title: Better process cleanup
description: Use `clean_tree = TRUE`.

title: revdep_check() should add revdep/ to .Rbuildignore
description:
tl;dr - Currently, `revdep_check()` creates a `revdep/` folder, but does not add that folder to `.Rbuildignore`.


I ran revdeps for the first time on a package right before submitting to CRAN. All was well, so I shipped it. I may or may not have accidentally shipped the entire `revdep/` folder with the package. 😈 This issue should prevent that from happening to others.

title: Setting R_LIB in .Renviron causes problems
description: This is the summary of a long slack thread between @gaborcsardi and me trying to figure out why CRAN discovered revdep problems that CRAN did not. The root cause seems to be me setting `R_LIB = ~/R` in my `.Renviron` and then having the development version installed there.

R crashes go unnoticed when they occur in both the CRAN and dev checks
description: Maybe the output could be grepped for things like *"An irrecoverable exception occurred. R is aborting now ..."*. When detected, should that go in a new section? In my case it meant something was wrong in my R library and I missed actual revdep failures because of that.

title: Helper to find all failures matching text
description: For packages with many revdeps failures, often there are just a few common causes. Once you've found one, it's useful to find all the others by looking for a match in the error text (e.g. `A continuous variable can not be mapped to linetype`)

title: Avoid WARNING noise: "Insufficient package version" and "This build time stamp is over a month old."
description:
Is there a way to _not_ report on the following WARNINGs?
```
Maintainer: ‘Alice Aliceson <alice@example.org>’

Insufficient package version (submitted: 0.8.0, existing: 0.8.0)

This build time stamp is over a month old.
```

They're often the only reason why a package end up in `problems.md`.

title: Common library for most frequently used packages
description:
I'd like to suggest a weaker version of #53: Before running the revdep checks, prepare a library with the most frequently used packages. I think we could reuse parts of #52 for this.

Yesterday I tried running tibble revdep checks on a 64-core machine, but the process appeared stuck in the beginning. I suspect this is because BH (and other heavy packages) are installed a countless number of times (BH: 233x for 265 downstream packages), and this resulted in overloading the disk. This is a waste of expensive CPU time (which goes unused during installation).

For simplicity, the common library would be populated by the main process just before starting revdepchecks. The packages to add there would be those that are used by at least, say, 2 * nproc or maybe 50 downstream packages. We can figure this out easily by looking at the dependency graph.

To maintain isolation, we symlink (or create junction points on Windows) to directories in the common library. So, the installation process for a package under check would first look at which packages are available in the common library, then create symlinks, and then install the remaining packages.

title: High MacOS Finder usage when running revdep_check()
description: My Finder window goes a bit crazy with process usage when I am running revdeps with multiple processes. I think because of all the new files created. It would be nice to exclude the `check/` folder from finder. From https://www.tekrevue.com/tip/three-ways-to-prevent-spotlight-from-indexing-items-on-your-mac/ it seems like folders with a `.noindex` extension are not indexed by Spotlight, so this might be a way to do this without having to manually exclude the folders by hand.

title: revdepcheck:::get_repos(bioc = TRUE) doesn't respect what's in getOption("repos")
description:
# Issue
`revdepcheck:::get_repos(bioc = TRUE)` prepends built-in Bioconductor URLs to any existing Bioconductor URLs already specified in `getOption("repos")`.   There are two problems with this:

1. Since it _prepends_ the built-in URLs, they will have higher priority than the ones specified in the `repos` option.
2. The built-in URLs are online repositories and because `revdepcheck` uses `options(warn = 2)` when installing packages, it will throw an error if those fail/cannot be accessed, e.g. due to lack of internet access.  Thus, it prevents using `revdepcheck` in offline mode.


# Example
With:
```r
> getOption("repos")
                                                                      CRAN 
                            "file:///netapp/home/hb/shared/r-mirrors/cran" 
                                                                  BioCsoft 
           "file:///netapp/home/hb/shared/r-mirrors/bioconductor/3.6/bioc" 
                                                                   BioCann 
"file:///netapp/home/hb/shared/r-mirrors/bioconductor/3.6/data/annotation" 
                                                                   BioCexp 
"file:///netapp/home/hb/shared/r-mirrors/bioconductor/3.6/data/experiment" 
```
we get:
```r
> repos <- revdepcheck:::get_repos(bioc = FALSE)
> repos
                                                                      CRAN 
                            "file:///netapp/home/hb/shared/r-mirrors/cran" 
                                                                  BioCsoft 
           "file:///netapp/home/hb/shared/r-mirrors/bioconductor/3.6/bioc" 
                                                                   BioCann 
"file:///netapp/home/hb/shared/r-mirrors/bioconductor/3.6/data/annotation" 
                                                                   BioCexp 
"file:///netapp/home/hb/shared/r-mirrors/bioconductor/3.6/data/experiment" 
```

So far so good, but:
```r
> repos <- revdepcheck:::get_repos(bioc = TRUE)
> repos
                                                                  BioCsoft 
                              "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.5/bioc" 
                                                                   BioCann 
                   "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.5/data/annotation" 
                                                                   BioCexp 
                   "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.5/data/experiment" 
                                                                 BioCextra 
                             "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.5/extra" 
                                                                      CRAN 
                            "file:///netapp/home/hb/shared/r-mirrors/cran" 
                                                                  BioCsoft 
           "file:///netapp/home/hb/shared/r-mirrors/bioconductor/3.6/bioc"
                                                                   BioCann 
"file:///netapp/home/hb/shared/r-mirrors/bioconductor/3.6/data/annotation" 
                                                                   BioCexp 
"file:///netapp/home/hb/shared/r-mirrors/bioconductor/3.6/data/experiment" 
```

PS. The `BioCextra` URL has been dropped in Bioconductor >= 3.6 (meaning it will also produce an error due to `warn = 2`).

# Patch
I'm happy to submit a PR that will make `revdepcheck:::get_repos(bioc = TRUE)` add only `BioC*` entries that are missing from `repos`.  I've got a fix ready locally.

title: Option to run checks from fastest to slowest
description:
With a large number of revdeps to check, it could be nice to run them in reverse order of (estimated) time it takes to complete the check, as opposed to alphabetical order. I'm guessing the check time info is available in the CRAN logs.
With this order, one could go through say 90% of the packages in a reasonable time. It's not purely for a psychological benefit (it feels more rewarding), as the decision to run the last few outliers could be made on a case-by-case basis (e.g. switch to a more performant machine, or email the maintainer and ask them to check it themselves, etc.)

Just a thought (while waiting for a list of 288 packages to go down from A to B, then C...).

title: revdep_install() gives Warning in rep.default(as.POSIXct(NA), length = length(dates))
description:
2017-09-21: The error produces only occurs when using `options(warnPartialMatchArgs = TRUE)`, otherwise it's just a warning.  I've updated the title to reflect this.

# Issue

```r
> revdepcheck::revdep_check()
── INIT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── Computing revdeps ──
── INSTALL ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 2 versions ──
Installing CRAN version of aroma.core
also installing the dependencies 'digest', 'base64enc', 'aroma.light', 'DNAcopy', 'globals', 'R.utils', 'R.filesets', 'R.devices', 'R.methodsS3', 'R.oo', 'R.cache', 'R.rsp', 'matrixStats', 'RColorBrewer', 'PSCBS', 'listenv', 'future'

Error in rep.default(as.POSIXct(NA), length = length(dates)) : 
  (converted from warning) partial argument match of 'length' to 'length.out'
In addition: Warning message:
call dbDisconnect() when finished working with a connection 
> traceback()
24: doWithOneRestart(return(expr), restart)
23: withOneRestart(expr, restarts[[1L]])
22: withRestarts({
        .Internal(.signalCondition(simpleWarning(msg, call), msg, 
            call))
        .Internal(.dfltWarn(msg, call))
    }, muffleWarning = function() NULL)
21: .signalSimpleWarning("partial argument match of 'length' to 'length.out'", 
        quote(rep.default(as.POSIXct(NA), length = length(dates))))
20: NextMethod()
19: rep.POSIXct(as.POSIXct(NA), length = length(dates))
18: rep(as.POSIXct(NA), length = length(dates))
17: parse_date(strsplit(built, ";")[[1]][3])
16: FUN(X[[i]], ...)
15: lapply(x, f)
14: unlist(lapply(x, f))
13: Filter(function(path) {
        desc <- file.path(path, "DESCRIPTION")
        if (!file.exists(desc)) 
            return(FALSE)
        dcf <- read.dcf(desc)
        if (!"Built" %in% colnames(dcf)) 
            return(FALSE)
        built <- dcf[, "Built"]
        build_date <- parse_date(strsplit(built, ";")[[1]][3])
        if (is.na(build_date)) 
            return(FALSE)
        build_date >= timestamp
    }, new_pkgs)
12: update_cache_binaries(destdir, warnings, lib, timestamp, args)
11: update_cache_safe(destdir, binaries, warnings, lib, timestamp, 
        args)
10: update_cache(destdir, add_built_binaries, warnings, lib, timestamp, 
        args)
9: install_packages(pkgname, quiet = quiet, repos = get_repos(bioc = TRUE))
8: force(code)
7: with_options(list(warn = 2), install_packages(pkgname, quiet = quiet, 
       repos = get_repos(bioc = TRUE)))
6: force(code)
5: with_libpaths(dir_find(pkg, "old"), with_options(list(warn = 2), 
       install_packages(pkgname, quiet = quiet, repos = get_repos(bioc = TRUE))))
4: force(code)
3: with_envvar(c(CRANCACHE_REPOS = "cran,bioc", CRANCACHE_QUIET = "yes"), 
       with_libpaths(dir_find(pkg, "old"), with_options(list(warn = 2), 
           install_packages(pkgname, quiet = quiet, repos = get_repos(bioc = TRUE)))))
2: revdep_install(pkg, quiet = quiet)
1: revdepcheck::revdep_check()
```


# Troubleshooting

This is because `revdep_install()` sets `options(warn = 2)` and `parsedate:::parse_date()` uses partial argument matching;

```r
> parsedate:::parse_date
function (dates, approx = TRUE) 
{
    result <- rep(as.POSIXct(NA), length = length(dates))
    dates <- trimws(dates)
    dates <- sapply(dates, replace.unparseable, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
    result[dates.to.parse(dates, result)] <- parse_iso_8601(dates[dates.to.parse(dates, 
        result)])
    result[dates.to.parse(dates, result)] <- parse_git(dates[dates.to.parse(dates, 
        result)], approx = approx)
    result[dates.to.parse(dates, result)] <- parse_rbase(dates[dates.to.parse(dates, 
        result)])
    result
}
<environment: namespace:parsedate>
```

# Fix

PR https://github.com/gaborcsardi/parsedate/pull/22 fixes the above issue.

title: `report_revdeps()` fails if there are `rcmdcheck_error` objects.
description:
I ran into a bunch of these with Bioconductor packages that failed to install, possibly related to #12.

These objects have a class of `rcmdcheck_error` and notably do not have values for `x$new$package` and `x$new$version` so `report_revdeps` fails with the following.

```r
Error in vapply(x, fun, ..., FUN.VALUE = character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE) :
  values must be length 1,
 but FUN(X[[6]]) result is length 0
```

It looks like the information is in the outer object however, so I will shortly send a PR to fix this.

title: first pass
description:
*posting this now while waiting for run to finish, will update ...*

running revdepcheck on the `bbmle` package with R version 3.4.0, MacOS, fresh install of revdepcheck/all packages updated
- warning messages (seem harmless but reporting them nonetheless
```
(11x) In rsqlite_fetch(res@ptr, n = n) :
  Don't need to call dbFetch() for statements, only for queries
(3x) In db_results(pkg, revdeps) :
  Some packages were not checked with both versions: ‘metaplus’
```
- I had a few packages fail to install due (I think) to timeouts in the installation process. In this case, we end up with PREPERR in the `status` column of data.sqlite ... and some metadata (version, maintainer) seems to disappear from data.sqlite.. Also, these packages don't show up in the running status report (unlike packages that timeout during checks, which have a "T"). Could this be handled more gracefully?
- might be helpful to remind user where the summaries live (i.e. `revdep/{README,problems.md}` when re-running `revdep_check` with all results cached 
- as far as I can tell (I may be badly mistaken) packages being checked get installed with all of their local packages in a dedicated library, then deleted after checking. I guess this is good for modularity, but it seems **very** expensive to install downstream dependencies many times (separately for every reverse dependency that requires it; e.g. imagine re-installing the entire tidyverse many, many times ... in my case, the `BH` package has been installed at least three times ...).  Is this a simple, justified tradeoff of computation time for simplicity/robustness/modularity? Would it be unreasonable to think of a way that the downstream packages needed could be shared in revdep/library ... ?
- the `revdep_maintainers()` is documented but not exported ...
- document status codes: I=installing, C=checking, D=downloading, I=installing, doubled chars [CC] refer to currently checking against both pkg versions?

title: Email template is duplicated when there are multiple results
description:
The `your_results` field may have length > 1 if there were issues in both examples and tests. Then `glue_data()` will duplicate the email template.

I worked around this by sticking this in `email_build()`:

```r
data$your_results <- glue::collapse(data$your_results)
```

* c: number of events present only with the new version
